extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants (SEC filers), their legal/compliance/ESG reporting teams, and assurance providers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final-rule requirements under Regulation S-K for disclosure of voluntary assurance over GHG emissions and the safe-harbor treatment of certain climate-related forward-looking statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger for Item 1506(e) voluntary-assurance disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any registrant that is not required to include a GHG emissions attestation report pursuant to Item 1506(a) must disclose certain information about the assurance engagement if the registrant's GHG emissions disclosure was voluntarily subject to assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is required whenever assurance services are voluntarily obtained by the registrant; the Commission declined to limit disclosure to situations where the registrant chooses to disclose the results, to avoid incentivizing nondisclosure of unfavorable results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of assurance service provider
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must identify the service provider of such assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The identity of the assurance provider is basic but important for investors, given the broad spectrum of providers (e.g., PCAOB-registered public accounting firms, unregistered public accounting firms, and other types of service providers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of assurance standard used
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose the assurance standard used by the service provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of the assurance standard enables investors to assess whether the standard is sufficiently developed; standards vary in robustness (some set by accreditation bodies with notice and comment), which affects comparability and investor assessment of reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of level and scope of assurance services
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must describe the level and scope of assurance services provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must clearly identify the level of assurance (e.g., limited vs. reasonable) and the scope (e.g., whether the assurance aligns with Scope 1 or Scope 2 emissions). This helps investors weigh reliance and determine whether assurance has enhanced reliability of the GHG disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of assurance results
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must briefly describe the results of the assurance services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring a brief description of results provides transparency about the reliability of any disclosed GHG emissions data and helps investors determine how much importance to place on that data when making investment decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of material business relationships/material professional services
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose whether the service provider has any material business relationships with or has provided any material professional services to the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule requires disclosure of material relationships rather than a registrant determination about whether such relationships "may lead to an impairment of the service provider's independence," because independence standards can vary by assurance standard. Disclosing material relationships plus the assurance standard helps investors evaluate impartiality and objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of oversight inspection programs and scope coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose whether the service provider is subject to any oversight inspection program, and if so, which program(s), and whether the assurance services over GHG emissions are included within the scope of authority of such oversight inspection program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure is not limited to oversight programs that inspect GHG assurance specifically; examples include the AICPA peer review program and the PCAOB inspection program. The rule considers assurance services to be within scope if it is possible for them to be inspected pursuant to the oversight program, even if not certain in a given inspection cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation to 'assurance' services (vs. verification/non-assurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require disclosure only about 'assurance' services — services performed in accordance with professional standards designed to provide assurance (e.g., an examination providing reasonable assurance or a review providing limited assurance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain attestation engagements that provide limited or reasonable assurance fall within scope; many 'verification' services and non-assurance services (e.g., agreed-upon procedures) are not designed to provide assurance and therefore are not covered by Item 1506(e). The Commission focused on assurance because investors are likely to place greater reliance on disclosures subject to assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of voluntary-assurance disclosure in filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should provide the disclosure required by Item 1506(e) in the same Commission filing and alongside the GHG emissions disclosure to which the voluntary assurance services relate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rules do not require placement within a separately captioned 'Climate-Related Disclosure' section; placement is left largely to the registrant but should be next to the GHG emissions disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing/furnishing of assurance reports and Rule 436 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 1506(e) does not require registrants to file or furnish any voluntary assurance reports to the Commission; Rule 436 is amended to provide that descriptions of assurance services under Item 1506(e) will not be considered part of the registration statement prepared or certified by an expert under sections 7 and 11 of the Securities Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amendment means registrants are not required to obtain written consent of the GHG emissions attestation provider under Securities Act section 7 for Item 1506(e) descriptions. A report by a GHG attestation provider covering Scopes 1/2/3 at a limited assurance level shall not be considered part of the registrant statement for sections 7 and 11 purposes under Rule 436(i)(1), subject to its terms. If a registrant files an assurance report that does not meet Rule 436(i)(1) (e.g., reasonable assurance) or voluntarily discloses more than Item 1506(e) requires, the exception may not apply and consents/liability under Section 11 may attach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1507: PSLRA safe-harbor designation for certain subpart 1500 disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures (other than historic facts) provided pursuant to specified subpart 1500 provisions are designated as 'forward-looking statements' for purposes of the PSLRA safe harbors: 17 CFR 229.1502(e) (transition plans); 17 CFR 229.1502(f) (scenario analysis); 17 CFR 229.1502(g) (internal carbon pricing); and 17 CFR 229.1504 (targets and goals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission is providing that the PSLRA safe harbors will apply to these forward-looking statements in connection with certain transactions and disclosures by certain issuers, notwithstanding some statutory exclusions. This is intended to avoid requiring disentangling of mixed factual and forward-looking content and to reduce compliance burden while protecting investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSLRA forward-looking statement types relevant to climate disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The PSLRA statutory definition of 'forward-looking statement' includes: projections of financial items; statements of management's plans and objectives for future operations; statements of future economic performance; statements of assumptions underlying such statements; and statements containing a projection or estimate specified by Commission rule or regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a statement in a subpart 1500 disclosure falls squarely within these types, parties may rely on existing PSLRA safe harbors, assuming other PSLRA requirements are met. The Commission also exercised PSLRA authority to extend protections where appropriate in the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Scope 3 safe harbor adopted (because no Scope 3 requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the final rules will not require disclosure of Scope 3 emissions from any registrant, the Commission is not adopting the proposed safe harbor for Scope 3 emissions disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission considered commenters' suggestions about broader or time-limited safe harbors but concluded that, given the final rules' scope, a Scope 3 safe harbor is unnecessary; commenters had various views (sunset periods, broader coverage, higher standards), which the Commission considered in deciding to apply PSLRA protections to certain forward-looking disclosures instead.
